question: Should OpenClaw replace the single `plugins.slots.memory` owner with supported memory role slots, or keep one memory owner and solve coexistence through narrower plugin APIs?
rationale: The request changes public configuration, plugin activation semantics, per-agent behavior, and memory/session state ownership, while VISION.md currently both welcomes plugin API design and states that only one memory plugin is active at a time.

options.title: Sponsor role-slot architecture
options.body: Review and repair `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504`, require explicit migration/doctor/status/upgrade proof, and make memory roles the supported config contract.

options.title: Keep one memory owner
options.body: Close this issue and the linked PR as not planned, then document the recommended memory path and the supported companion-plugin surfaces for non-owner behavior.

options.title: Narrow to coexistence hooks
options.body: Reject a broad taxonomy for now and open smaller API work for specific gaps such as dreaming, user-model prompt sections, or capture hooks alongside the active recall provider.

recommendation.title: Sponsor role-slot architecture
recommendation.body: Review and repair `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504`, require explicit migration/doctor/status/upgrade proof, and make memory roles the supported config contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent repo history and VISION.md ownership signals make `steipete` the best available routing candidate for the product/API direction choice.
